description.narrative:
This project marks the second phase of a three-part initiative by Oxfam Novib and CIRAD to test innovative collaboration models andtools for scaling equitable partnerships between farmers and researchers. Together with P4D partners, Oxfam Novib and CIRAD envision P4D as a collaborative, locally-driven platform for farmers, researchers, NGOs, and other stakeholders. The platform will (a) foster regular exchanges of ideas and methodologies, (b) share data and innovations, (c) build synergies across expertise and projects, and (d) collectively fundraise and influence donor agendas through national and cross- regional networks. To achieve this, Oxfam andCIRAD propose coordinating the platform during a one-year pilot, creating an initial bridge between organizations and projects while pooling resources and diverse expertise. P4D is structured with national and regional leadership, facilitated by a secretariat (Oxfam and CIRAD) and five pathway leads, representing the organizations that took part in the 2023 workshops in Burkina Faso and Uganda, to be elected by P4D members.
Content-wise P4D is organized around five pathways which resulted from a co-creation process in the exploratory phase of this project during 2023: (1) collaborative research for agrobiodiversity management, focusing on research methods and innovations to counter genetic diversity loss; (2) local value chain development to improve farmers' incomes through stronger market linkages and supportive policies; (3) data management and sharing to create robust knowledge exchange systems; (4) advocacy and policy work to promote legislative changes that empower farmers; and (5) gender and social inclusion to ensure marginalized groups have a voice in all activities. Each pathway is envisioned to build linkages among stakeholders, promote inclusive decision-making, and amplify smallholder farmers' voices, ensuring that local voices and priorities remain central to the initiative. P4D aims to integrate both research and implementation across its five pathways, requiring farmer organizations to partner with research institutes. Proposals will be co-developed by FOs and NARS, ensuring research aligns with farmers' priorities. P4D, in the 1 year pilot,also addresses a research question on whether such a network, within a year, can generate sufficient momentum and energy to sustainjoint actions and attract diverse funding sources beyond its initial phase.
Activities in P4D will be designed by and for local farmer associations, researchers, and civil society, aiming to support diverse farmer groups by capitalizing on prior collaborations, networks of exchange, participatory research, and peer-to-peer learning. This approach aims to transform individual initiatives intointegrated programs linked with other like-minded collaborations, allowing for knowledge sharing, adaptation to evolving challenges, and increased influence. P4D aligns closely with CRFS Strategy 1, which focuses on accelerating local and regional food systems transformation. The initiative fosters farmer-centered research, action, and influence, aiming to enhance agroecological practices anddrive systemic change from the ground up. By supporting strong local networks and partnerships, P4D directly contributes to transforming food systems through collaborative, inclusive approaches that can be adapted and scaled regionally and globally.

participating-org.narrative:
CIRAD (French Agricultural Research Centre for International Development) works with its partners to build knowledge and solutions and invent resilient farming systems for a more sustainable, inclusive world. It mobilizes science, innovation and trainingin order to achieve the Sustainable Development Goals. Its expertise supports the entire range of stakeholders, from producers to public policymakers, to foster biodiversity protection, agroecological transitions, food system sustainability, health (of plants, animals and ecosystems), sustainable development of rural territories, and their resilience to climate change.
CIRAD was founded in 1984 as a public establishment (EPIC), following a merger of French tropical agricultural research organizations,and is under the joint authority of the Ministry of Higher Education, Research and Innovation and the Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs. As such, it supports French science diplomacy operations.
CIRAD works in some fifty countries on every continent, thanks to the expertise of its 1650 staff members, including 1140 scientists, backed by a global network of some 200 partners.
